question: Does matching Kendall tau suffice for joint extremes, and does conditional Monte Carlo resolve finite-threshold coexceedance more precisely than direct simulation?
baseline: Direct latent elliptical simulation at identical n, q, rho, model, and 80 independent replicates. Different RNG streams by method. Equal n is not equal CPU budget; time and tracked peak memory are reported separately.
reference: Two 1D adaptive quadratures: truncated marginal survival coordinates and latent x on [threshold,infinity). Shared scipy special-function library, different integral coordinates; not formal interval certification.
scope: Known bivariate copula parameters and exact marginal exceedance probability; no estimation, time dependence, credit-loss capital validation or universal empirical superiority claim.
hardware: Recorded at execution. One BLAS/OMP thread; timed calls include RNG; tracemalloc peak in separate calls, not RSS; no warmup, fixed order.
